key_insight: Distributed quantum-centric supercomputing combines smaller quantum calculations with generative learning to reconstruct intermolecular electronic structure at lower computational cost.
engineering_relevance: Partitioning molecular systems can reduce per-subproblem qubit requirements, circuit depth, sampling budgets, and classical diagonalization demands.
method: Solve molecular fragments in parallel using physics-informed generative sample-based quantum diagonalization (PIGen-SQD).
Optimize local-to-global bit assignments to assemble a mapped tensor product state.
Use a second generative module to identify dominant global configurations and recover inter-fragment correlations.
evidence_signal: For water and formamide dimers, the abstract reports up to 95% smaller diagonalization dimensions and an order-of-magnitude improvement in energy accuracy over conventional SQD; a 120-qubit water hexamer was partitioned into six 20-qubit subsystems with excellent agreement with classical references.
watch_item: The hexamer reconstruction uses a dimeric approximation, leaving accuracy for systems with stronger higher-order inter-fragment correlations uncertain.
paper_title: Distributed Quantum-Centric Supercomputing with Multi-Layered Generative Learning for Intermolecular Interactions
